steps.intent: The Russian draft prioritizes an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, unimpeded access, the release of hostages and protection of Palestinian civilians, while reaffirming the two-State solution and the illegality of settlements. The most difficult issues will be balancing condemnation of the 7 October attacks with opposition to legitimizing Israel’s military operation; we have used generic language on terrorism and self-defence to attract Western abstentions or support and prevent a veto. Another point of contention will be the demand to reverse forced displacement and the reference to occupation, which the United States and some Western members may seek to dilute. We will resist weakening the ceasefire and humanitarian access provisions while seeking the nine votes and P5 unity necessary for adoption.

messages.Albania: Albania cannot support the text as drafted because it does not explicitly condemn Hamas's terrorist attacks, including those of 7 October, and fails to affirm clearly Israel's right to self-defence. We ask the penholder to add these red-line elements and to replace the call for an immediate ceasefire with humanitarian pauses and corridors, while retaining strong humanitarian access and hostage-release provisions. With these changes, Albania would be prepared to support the resolution.
messages.Brazil: Brazil supports the draft’s humanitarian ceasefire, humanitarian access, hostage release and two-State reaffirmation. To be able to support the text, Brazil needs an explicit condemnation of the terrorist attacks by Hamas on 7 October, not merely a date reference, and a clear call for rescinding the evacuation order affecting civilians in northern Gaza. We are ready to work with the penholder and all members to bridge these points.
messages.China: China supports the core of the draft and welcomes the Russian Federation's initiative for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire. We ask that OP4 explicitly demand an end to the collective punishment and blockade of Gaza and the opening of the Rafah crossing under credible humanitarian guarantees. With this improvement, China is ready to support the text and urges the Council to act promptly to avert a wider humanitarian catastrophe.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador supports the draft's humanitarian focus and its balanced reaffirmation of self-defence and international law, but cannot support it as presented without an explicit condemnation of the Hamas terrorist attacks of 7 October. We also ask the penholder to make humanitarian access operational through a UN-coordinated notification and deconfliction mechanism, so that convoys and medical evacuations can move safely. We are ready to work constructively to bridge these points.
messages.France: France welcomes the draft's focus on humanitarian access and the protection of civilians and supports the Council speaking out clearly. However, France cannot support a text that does not unequivocally name and condemn Hamas's terrorist attacks of 7 October and hostage-taking; this is a red line. We also ask that the ceasefire language be adjusted to a humanitarian truce and pauses, consistent with the need to protect civilians while preserving Israel's right to self-defence under international law.
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports the draft resolution as a balanced and urgent response to the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza. We call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, the release of all hostages, and strict respect for international humanitarian law. We urge the Council to speak with one voice and to avoid any further delay in addressing the protection of civilians and the resumption of a credible political process towards a two-State solution.
messages.Ghana: Ghana supports the draft as a basis and welcomes its calls for a humanitarian ceasefire, unhindered humanitarian access and the release of hostages. To ensure clear condemnation of terrorism, we ask that OP6 explicitly attribute the 7 October attacks to Hamas. With this change, Ghana is prepared to support the text.
messages.Japan: Japan cannot support the current text as drafted because it does not explicitly condemn Hamas's terrorist attacks of 7 October. We request that OP6 name Hamas and other terrorist groups and explicitly condemn hostage-taking, and that OP3 clarify that all hostages held by Hamas must be released immediately with ICRC access. With these changes, Japan is prepared to support the resolution.
messages.Malta: Malta supports the draft's humanitarian ceasefire, humanitarian access and two-State objective, but it cannot support a text that does not explicitly condemn the Hamas terrorist attacks of 7 October. We therefore ask the penholder to name Hamas in OP6, add ICRC access to hostages in OP3, and ensure OP4 provides for a UN-coordinated, unconditional humanitarian corridor. With these changes Malta is prepared to support the resolution.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique supports the draft as a balanced basis for Council action. We welcome its call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and a two-State solution. We urge all members to unite behind this text without delay.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland supports the Council’s urgent call for a humanitarian ceasefire and the protection of civilians. We can support this text if it explicitly names Hamas’s terrorist attacks of 7 October and indiscriminate rocket attacks against Israel, and if it demands ICRC access to all hostages. We also ask the penholder to strengthen OP4 on sustained humanitarian access, including Rafah, other crossings, conflict lines and safe humanitarian convoys.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The UAE co-sponsored this draft and supports its adoption as it stands. We urge the Council to act swiftly to demand an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, unhindered humanitarian access, the unconditional release of all hostages and the protection of civilians under international humanitarian law. The text is balanced and should remain focused on de-escalation and the two-State solution.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK welcomes the draft's focus on humanitarian access and protection of civilians. However, we could not support the text as it stands: it must explicitly condemn Hamas's terrorist attacks of 7 October, affirm Israel's right to self-defence, and avoid a ceasefire that would allow Hamas to regroup. We ask the penholder to incorporate the changes below.
messages.United States of America: The United States cannot support this draft as written. It must explicitly condemn Hamas's terrorist attacks and hostage-taking, and it cannot call for an immediate ceasefire; the Council should instead support humanitarian pauses and corridors. We also need explicit affirmation of Israel's inherent right to self-defence. Without these changes, the United States will vote against the text.

It is expected to garner broad support but face a US veto due to the retained ceasefire and refusal to single out Israel's right to self-defence.

messages.Albania: Albania welcomes the inclusion of OP6 naming Hamas and condemning its terrorist attacks, as well as OP3 on hostages. We cannot accept a text that does not explicitly recognize Israel's right to defend itself against Hamas terrorism; we therefore ask to amend OP2 along the lines previously proposed. We also continue to prefer humanitarian pauses and corridors rather than an immediate ceasefire in OP1, so as not to prejudge Israel's right to self-defence. With those changes, Albania is ready to support the draft.
messages.Brazil: Brazil supports the current text as revised. We welcome the explicit condemnation of Hamas’s terrorist attacks and the integration of our request on rescinding the evacuation order and ensuring safe and voluntary return. The humanitarian situation is catastrophic, and the Council must act without further delay to secure humanitarian access, protect civilians, release all hostages and preserve the two-State solution.
messages.China: China supports the revised draft as balanced and responsive to the emergency. We welcome the acceptance of our OP4 amendment on ending collective punishment and the blockade and opening Rafah under credible humanitarian guarantees. China urges the Council to act with unity, prioritize an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, safe and unhindered access, release of all hostages, protection of civilians, and a return to the two-State solution based on the 1967 lines with East Jerusalem as the capital. We oppose forced displacement and regional escalation.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador supports the current draft and thanks the penholder for incorporating the explicit condemnation of the 7 October terrorist attacks by Hamas and the humanitarian notification and deconfliction mechanism. The text now addresses the catastrophic humanitarian situation, the need to protect civilians, the release of hostages and the resumption of a credible political horizon based on the two-State solution. Ecuador urges all Council members to unite and adopt this resolution without delay.
messages.France: France welcomes the revision, especially the explicit condemnation of Hamas's terrorist attacks and the reference to hostages. We continue to believe the Council should call for an immediate humanitarian truce and humanitarian pauses leading to a cessation of hostilities rather than a durable ceasefire. With that adjustment, France is ready to support the text.
messages.Gabon: La délégation gabonaise soutient le texte révisé, qui répond à l’urgence humanitaire à Gaza et réaffirme le droit international. Nous saluons la condamnation des attaques terroristes du Hamas, l’appel à la libération des otages et le rejet du déplacement forcé. Nous n’avons pas de modification à demander et appelons le Conseil à adopter rapidement ce texte pour mettre fin aux souffrances des civils.
messages.Ghana: Ghana thanks the Russian Federation for accepting the amendment to OP6 explicitly naming Hamas’s terrorist attacks of 7 October. The current text reflects Ghana’s priorities: an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and hospitals, release of hostages, and a credible path back to a two-State solution. Ghana therefore supports the draft as it stands and urges the Council to speak with one voice.
messages.Japan: Japan welcomes the incorporation of our previous requests naming Hamas and ensuring ICRC access to hostages. We can support the revised text, but we ask that OP4 avoid the legal characterization 'collective punishment and blockade' and instead call concretely for the immediate lifting of restrictions on humanitarian access. This preserves balance while addressing the humanitarian emergency.
messages.Malta: Malta thanks the penholder for accepting its key requests, in particular naming Hamas and its terrorist attacks, guaranteeing ICRC access to hostages, and ensuring a UN-coordinated humanitarian corridor. The revised text now clearly condemns terrorism, addresses the catastrophic humanitarian situation, and reaffirms the two-State solution. Malta therefore supports the draft as it stands and urges the Council to speak with one voice.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique supports the current draft as a necessary call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, protection of civilians, unhindered humanitarian access and the release of all hostages. We believe the Council must speak with urgency and unity in the face of the catastrophic situation in Gaza. Mozambique therefore supports the text as presented and urges all members to support it.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland supports the revised draft. The explicit condemnation of Hamas’s terrorist attacks, the demand for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages with ICRC access, and the strengthened humanitarian access provisions address our key concerns. We urge all members to support the text so that the Council can speak with one voice to alleviate the catastrophic humanitarian situation and protect civilians in accordance with international humanitarian law.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates supports the revised draft as a co-sponsor and believes it provides a balanced basis for Council action. We welcome the clear calls for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, unhindered humanitarian access, the release of all hostages, rejection of forced displacement, and protection of civilians and medical facilities. We urge all Council members to support the text and call for its prompt adoption.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom welcomes the explicit condemnation of Hamas' terrorist attacks and the call for release of hostages. However, we cannot support the text without an explicit reaffirmation of Israel's right to self-defence under Article 51, and we remain opposed to an unconditional ceasefire that would tie Israel's hands while hostages are held and Hamas continues attacks. We therefore ask the penholder to reflect these changes, and to replace the problematic 'collective punishment and blockade' language with clear calls for IHL compliance and humanitarian access.
messages.United States of America: We welcome the explicit condemnation of Hamas in OP6, but the United States cannot support a text that calls for a ceasefire rather than humanitarian pauses and corridors. OP1 must be replaced as proposed, and OP2 must explicitly affirm Israel's inherent right to self-defence. We also cannot accept language characterizing Israel's actions as collective punishment; OP4 should focus on humanitarian access and the sustained opening of crossings.

The US veto is expected to block adoption.

reasons.Albania: Albania’s red-line request for explicit recognition of Israel’s right to self-defence against terrorism was not accepted, and the original ceasefire language was retained. Its pro-Israel, pro-US alignment and actual Council practice support an abstention rather than a yes vote.
reasons.Brazil: Brazil’s negotiation position was support, and the draft aligns with Brazil’s established emphasis on a humanitarian ceasefire, protection of civilians, condemnation of terrorism and all violence, and a two-State solution. Voting in favour is consistent with Brazil’s record and foreign policy priorities on this agenda item.
reasons.China: China supported the Russian draft’s ceasefire and humanitarian provisions, consistent with its pro-Palestinian and Gaza de-escalation position. Its explanation of vote was delivered after the vote, not before.
reasons.Ecuador: Ecuador's last negotiation position was support with no changes requested, and the draft aligns with Ecuador's emphasis on humanitarian ceasefire, civilian protection, condemnation of terrorism and the two-State solution. Therefore Ecuador votes in favour and explains its vote.
reasons.France: France’s sole requested change in the last round—replacing “humanitarian ceasefire” with “humanitarian truce and pauses” in OP1—was rejected. At this date, France is not prepared to endorse a full ceasefire and maintains that humanitarian relief must be pursued without undermining Israel’s right to self-defence.
reasons.Gabon: Gabon consistently supports humanitarian ceasefires and a two-State solution; its prior practice and last-round support indicate a yes vote. It is likely to explain its vote after the vote rather than before, so no pre-vote statement.
reasons.Ghana: Ghana indicated support in the final negotiation round with no requested changes, and the draft aligns with its foreign policy priorities on humanitarian access, civilian protection, and a two-State solution.
reasons.Japan: Japan’s actual vote on the Russian draft on 16 October 2023 was against, aligning with the US and other G7 members in opposing an immediate ceasefire and problematic characterizations, while supporting humanitarian pauses instead.
reasons.Malta: Malta’s negotiation position was support with no requested changes, and the final draft includes its core priorities on humanitarian ceasefire, civilian protection, hostages, and the two-State solution. Therefore, Malta would vote in favour.
reasons.Mozambique: Mozambique supported the draft without requested changes in the negotiation round and, consistent with its emphasis on humanitarian ceasefire, international law, civilian protection, and a two-State solution, would vote yes.
reasons.Russian Federation: As the submitting delegation, Russia votes in favour and explains its support, consistent with its push for a humanitarian ceasefire and its criticism of collective punishment in Gaza.
reasons.Switzerland: Switzerland’s last negotiation position was support with no requested changes, and the text now includes the key Swiss priorities: condemnation of Hamas’s attacks, hostage release, self-defence, humanitarian ceasefire and access, and protection of civilians. This is consistent with Switzerland’s foreign policy, so it votes in favour.
reasons.United Arab Emirates: UAE co-sponsored the draft and its stated position was support; it aligns with UAE’s emphasis on humanitarian ceasefire, aid access, hostage release, civilian protection, and the two-State solution.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK historically voted against the Russian draft on 16 October 2023 because it was unbalanced and did not adequately reflect Israel’s right to self-defence or condition a ceasefire on hostages’ release and an end to Hamas attacks.
reasons.United States of America: The United States at this date opposed the Russian draft because it called for an immediate ceasefire and contained unbalanced language, despite supporting humanitarian access and hostage release. The delegation would vote against and would explain its vote before the Council.

before.Albania: Thank you, Mr. President. Albania unequivocally condemns the terrorist attacks by Hamas and other terrorist groups against Israel on 7 October and calls for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. We support urgent humanitarian access and the protection of civilians in Gaza. However, we cannot support this draft because it still does not explicitly affirm Israel’s inherent right to defend itself against terrorism and retains a formulation on an immediate and durable ceasefire that risks constraining that right. For these reasons, Albania will abstain.
before.Brazil: Brazil will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza requires an immediate ceasefire, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, and the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure. Brazil reiterates its condemnation of the terrorist attacks by Hamas on 7 October and of all acts of violence against civilians, and stresses that all counter-terrorism measures must comply with international law, including international humanitarian law. We call for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, the rescission of orders that would displace civilians, and full respect for international humanitarian law. The Council must act with unity to prevent further suffering and regional escalation, and to preserve the prospect of a two-State solution based on the 1967 lines.
before.Ecuador: Ecuador will vote in favour. The humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza demands that this Council act without further delay. We condemn all acts of terrorism, including the attacks by Hamas on 7 October, and all attacks against civilians. We call for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, a humanitarian ceasefire, unimpeded humanitarian access, and the protection of civilians, hospitals and United Nations facilities. International humanitarian law must be respected by all parties. Ecuador reiterates that the only viable path is a two-State solution based on the 1967 lines, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace within secure and recognised borders. We urge all parties and regional actors to exercise restraint and prevent any further escalation.
before.France: France condemns in the strongest terms the terrorist attacks committed by Hamas and other terrorist groups on 7 October, and calls for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. France is deeply concerned by the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and calls for safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access, the protection of civilians and humanitarian personnel, and full respect for international humanitarian law. France has consistently called for a humanitarian truce and humanitarian pauses to allow assistance to reach civilians, while preserving Israel’s right to self-defence. We regret that the draft before us calls for an immediate, durable and fully respected ceasefire, rather than the humanitarian truce we proposed. That is why France will vote against the draft. We remain ready to work with all Council members on a balanced text that can be adopted and that responds to the urgent needs of the civilian population.
before.Japan: Japan thanks the delegation of the Russian Federation for its efforts. Japan unequivocally condemns the terrorist attacks by Hamas and other terrorist groups on 7 October, and we reiterate our call for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. We recognize Israel’s inherent right to self-defence in accordance with international law, and we remain deeply concerned about the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza. Japan has consistently supported humanitarian pauses to allow safe and unimpeded humanitarian access. However, the draft before us calls for an immediate, durable ceasefire without adequate sequencing or guarantees, and it retains language that characterizes Israel’s legitimate actions as collective punishment. Such language is not balanced and does not reflect the complex realities on the ground. For these reasons, Japan cannot support the draft resolution in its current form and will vote against it.
before.Mozambique: Thank you, Mr. President. Mozambique votes in favour of the draft resolution before the Council. The catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza requires an immediate and durable humanitarian ceasefire, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. We condemn all violence and acts of terrorism against civilians, and we reaffirm that international humanitarian law must be respected by all parties. Mozambique also reiterates the urgency of a two-State solution based on the 1967 lines and of credible negotiations. It is for these reasons that we support this draft resolution.
before.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation has submitted this draft because the Security Council cannot remain silent while Gaza faces a humanitarian catastrophe. We call for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, the release of all hostages, protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and strict compliance with international humanitarian law. The text is balanced: it condemns all violence and terrorism, rejects forced displacement, and reaffirms the two-State solution based on the 1967 lines. We urge all members to support the draft and to place the saving of civilian lives above political calculations.
before.Switzerland: Switzerland will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We condemn in the strongest terms the terrorist attacks by Hamas and other terrorist groups on 7 October, demand the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, and affirm Israel’s right to self-defence in accordance with international law. At the same time, the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza requires an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and respect for international humanitarian law by all parties. Switzerland rejects forced displacement and reiterates its support for a two-State solution based on the 1967 lines. We call on all parties to implement this resolution in good faith.
before.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The Council cannot remain silent while civilians in Gaza face an unfolding humanitarian catastrophe. We support the demand for an immediate, durable humanitarian ceasefire, safe and unhindered humanitarian access—including through the Rafah crossing—the unconditional release of all hostages, the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and the rejection of any forced displacement of Palestinians. The draft also reaffirms that all counter-terrorism measures must comply with international law and confirms the centrality of a two-State solution based on the 1967 lines. We urge all members to support this text so that the Council can speak with one voice and help prevent further loss of life and regional escalation.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Thank you, Mr. President. The United Kingdom condemns the appalling terrorist attacks by Hamas on 7 October and calls again for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. Israel has the right to defend itself against terrorism, in accordance with international law, and all parties must protect civilians and ensure rapid, safe and unhindered humanitarian access. We have engaged constructively on this draft, but it still does not reflect the balance required by the Council: it does not clearly affirm Israel’s right to self-defence as we requested, and it calls for a ceasefire without making that contingent on the release of hostages and an end to Hamas’s attacks. For those reasons, the United Kingdom will vote against this draft resolution.
before.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States has engaged in good faith to find a text that can unite the Council. We continue to support urgent humanitarian access, the protection of civilians, and the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. But the draft before us fails the fundamental test of balance and realism. It demands an immediate ceasefire while Hamas continues to hold hostages, fire rockets, and put civilians at risk. It does not adequately affirm Israel’s inherent right to self-defence, and it retains language that wrongly characterizes Israel’s efforts to defend its people as collective punishment. We asked for changes that would have focused the Council on humanitarian pauses and corridors rather than a ceasefire that would allow Hamas to regroup and rearm. Those changes were not made. For that reason, the United States cannot support this resolution. We will vote against it.

after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of the draft resolution before the Council. The situation in Gaza is extremely grave. We are deeply shocked and saddened by the continued escalation, the heavy civilian casualties and the catastrophic humanitarian consequences. China condemns all acts of violence against civilians and all violations of international humanitarian law. We call for an immediate ceasefire, the opening of safe and unimpeded humanitarian corridors, and the protection of civilians, hospitals and United Nations facilities. We support the release of all hostages and the humane treatment of all detainees in accordance with international law.

The Palestinian question is at the core of the Middle East issue. The legitimate national rights of the Palestinian people must be respected. The only viable way out is the two-State solution, based on the 1967 borders, with East Jerusalem as the capital of an independent State of Palestine, living side by side with Israel in peace. China supports all efforts conducive to de-escalation and to resuming credible peace negotiations.

China regrets that the Council has not been able to adopt this draft. At this critical moment, the Security Council should not remain silent or divided. Its actions must help stop the fighting, alleviate the humanitarian disaster, protect civilians and prevent a wider regional conflict. We urge all parties to exercise restraint, put the safety of civilians and the prospects for peace first, and support the Council in speaking with one voice. China will continue to play a constructive role in promoting ceasefire, humanitarian relief and a just and lasting settlement of the Palestinian question.
after.Gabon:
Mr. President,

Gabon voted in favour of the draft resolution before the Council because the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza demands that this Council act without delay. We deeply regret that the Security Council was unable to adopt the text, despite the urgent need to save civilian lives, alleviate suffering and prevent further regional escalation.

Gabon condemns all acts of terrorism and all violence against civilians. We call for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages and for their humane treatment in accordance with international humanitarian law. We also call for an immediate and durable humanitarian ceasefire, safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access throughout the Gaza Strip, including through the Rafah crossing, and the protection of civilians, hospitals, medical personnel, United Nations facilities and humanitarian workers.

International humanitarian law must be respected by all parties. We reject any forced displacement of Palestinian civilians and any attempt to alter the demographic composition, character and status of the Palestinian territory occupied since 1967. The evacuation order for northern Gaza must be rescinded, and displaced persons must be able to return safely and voluntarily.

Gabon remains convinced that the only path to a just and lasting peace is a two-State solution, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace and security within secure and internationally recognized borders, based on the 1967 lines and the relevant United Nations resolutions. We call on all members of the Council to overcome their divisions, to speak with one voice and to support credible negotiations and all diplomatic efforts aimed at ending the violence and restoring hope for peace. The Council cannot remain silent in the face of such suffering.
after.Ghana:
Mr. President,

Ghana voted in favour of the draft resolution before the Council. We did so out of a deep conviction that the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza, and the tragic loss of civilian life in Israel and Gaza, require the Security Council to act with urgency, unity and a clear voice.

Ghana supported this text because it condemned all violence and acts of terrorism against civilians, including the terrorist attacks by Hamas and other groups on 7 October; demanded the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages; called for an immediate, durable and fully respected humanitarian ceasefire; demanded safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access, including through the Rafah crossing; rejected forced displacement; and reaffirmed the centrality of international humanitarian law and the two-State solution based on the 1967 lines.

Ghana regrets that this Council has again been unable to adopt a resolution at a moment when civilians are enduring immense suffering. The Security Council cannot remain silent in the face of this humanitarian catastrophe. We call on all members to redouble efforts to find common ground, to prevent regional escalation, to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure, to ensure humanitarian access, and to create the conditions for a just, lasting and comprehensive peace in which Israelis and Palestinians can live side by side in peace and security.
after.Malta:
Thank you, Mr. President.

Malta voted in favour of this draft resolution because the Security Council cannot remain silent in the face of the catastrophic humanitarian situation in Gaza and the grave risk of further regional escalation. Malta unequivocally condemns the terrorist attacks by Hamas and other terrorist groups on 7 October and calls for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. We reaffirm Israel’s right to self-defence in accordance with international law, and we stress that all parties must respect international humanitarian law and protect civilians, hospitals, United Nations facilities and humanitarian personnel.

We supported the call for an immediate, durable and fully respected humanitarian ceasefire leading to a cessation of hostilities, and for humanitarian pauses to allow safe, rapid and unhindered humanitarian access. We reject any forced displacement of Palestinian civilians and any attempt to alter the demographic composition, character and status of the Palestinian territory occupied since 1967. Malta remains convinced that the only sustainable path is a two-State solution based on the 1967 lines, with Israel and Palestine living side by side in peace within secure and recognised borders.

Malta deeply regrets that the Council has again been unable to adopt a text on this urgent matter. The humanitarian imperative must transcend political divisions. We urge all members to continue working towards a united Council response that saves lives, ensures humanitarian access, protects civilians, secures the release of hostages and preserves the prospects for peace.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr President,

The Russian Federation voted in favour of the draft resolution because it reflected the most urgent task before the Security Council — to stop the bloodshed and prevent a further humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza. We deeply regret that this draft was not adopted, solely because of the negative votes of three permanent members — France, the United Kingdom and the United States. By blocking this text, they have once again prevented the Council from speaking with a unified voice at a moment when civilians are dying and the humanitarian situation is deteriorating by the hour.

We reject the claim that the draft resolution was not balanced. It clearly condemned all violence and terrorism, including the Hamas attacks of 7 October, demanded the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages, reaffirmed the inherent right of States to self-defence under Article 51 of the Charter, and stressed that all counter-terrorism measures must comply with international humanitarian law. At the same time, it called for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, safe and unhindered humanitarian access, protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and the immediate lifting of the blockade of Gaza. It also rejected any forced displacement of Palestinian civilians and reaffirmed the two-State solution based on the 1967 lines.

Those who voted against this resolution cannot escape their responsibility. Their vetoes do not create peace; they only prolong the suffering of civilians and erode the credibility of the Security Council. We call on all members to support the objective of an immediate ceasefire and to work for the swift resumption of credible negotiations on the Palestinian-Israeli settlement. The Russian Federation will continue to make every effort to ensure that the Security Council discharges its Charter responsibilities and acts to save lives.
after.United Arab Emirates:
Mr. President,

The United Arab Emirates regrets that the Security Council has been unable to adopt this draft resolution, which we co-sponsored and supported. At a moment when civilians in Gaza are facing a humanitarian catastrophe, the Council should have sent an unequivocal message in favour of protecting civilians, ensuring safe and unhindered humanitarian access—including through the Rafah crossing—securing the unconditional release of all hostages, and rejecting any forced displacement of Palestinians.

The failure to act does not diminish the obligations of all parties under international humanitarian law, nor does it remove the urgent need for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and a sustained humanitarian response. We call on all members to overcome divisions, prevent further regional escalation, and work collectively to alleviate the suffering of civilians and preserve the prospect of a two-State solution based on the 1967 lines. The UAE will continue to support all credible diplomatic and humanitarian efforts to that end.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Thank you, Mr. President. The United Kingdom voted against this draft because it was not balanced and did not reflect the gravity of the terrorist threat that Israel faces. We condemn in the strongest terms Hamas’s appalling terrorist attacks on 7 October, and we reiterate our call for the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. Israel has the right to defend itself against terrorism, in accordance with international law. At the same time, the humanitarian situation in Gaza is dire and must be addressed urgently. We continue to call for humanitarian pauses to allow safe, rapid and unhindered access for aid, for the protection of civilians and civilian infrastructure, and for full respect for international humanitarian law by all parties. The United Kingdom regrets that the Council has again been unable to unite around a balanced text. We remain ready to work with all members on a resolution that clearly condemns Hamas’s terrorism, demands the release of hostages, affirms Israel’s right to self-defence, addresses the humanitarian catastrophe, rejects forced displacement, and keeps alive the prospect of a two-State solution based on the 1967 lines. Thank you.
after.United States of America: Mr. President, the United States takes the floor after this vote to explain our opposition. We voted against this draft not because we are indifferent to the humanitarian catastrophe unfolding in Gaza, but because the Council must not adopt a one-sided text that fails to confront the reality of Hamas’s terrorist attack on 7 October. This draft does not clearly affirm Israel’s inherent right to self-defence. It does not adequately name Hamas’s terrorism and hostage-taking. And it uses language that wrongly characterizes Israel’s legitimate efforts to protect its people. We cannot support a text that could be read as tying Israel’s hands while Hamas continues to hold hostages, fire rockets, and endanger civilians. The United States strongly supports safe, rapid, and unhindered humanitarian access, humanitarian pauses, the protection of civilians, and the immediate and unconditional release of all hostages. We are working intensively with partners to get assistance to civilians in Gaza, including through the Rafah crossing, and to prevent a wider regional escalation. We remain committed to a two-State solution and to a balanced Council response that condemns Hamas’s terrorism, recognizes Israel’s right to defend itself in accordance with international law, demands the release of all hostages, and advances real humanitarian action. We urge all members to work with us on a text that can actually be implemented and that protects innocent civilians.
